title: EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge: Reacting to the 10 most-bought players
text: We are only days away from a new edition of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. It feels like yesterday when we created the game back in 2004. That means we're now entering the 23rd edition, and the Fantasy Challenge is more popular than ever. It's safe to say the game has developed a bit of a basketball cult following over the years, which is fantastic. We're one big Fantasy Challenge family. That makes me incredibly proud, so thank you, Fantasy managers. One of my favorite things about the start of the season is how unpredictable it can be. Some players I expect to dominate fail spectacularly, while some of the picks I dismiss end up becoming Fantasy gold. That gave me an idea: why not look at the Top 10 most-bought players and give my honest opinion on each one? Let's play this game. I'll go from least-owned to most-owned, all the way up to whoever's No. 1, and I haven't seen the list, honest to God. I'll simply be given a player's name, their ownership percentage, and asked to react. If you follow the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast, you already know my stance: if Sasha Vezenkov isn't No. 1, someone out there is making a mistake. ### 10. Mario Saint-Supery, Valencia Basket (4.7 credits, owned by 14.9%) This makes perfect sense. [Mario Saint-Supery] is very affordable, is expected to play significant minutes and should increase in value right away. He's in all of my teams, so I'm certainly not surprised to see him here. Good move, everyone. ### 9. Jean Montero, Olympiacos Piraeus (12.8 credits, owned by 15.0%) I don't love this pick. [Jean Montero] will probably need some time to settle in and play his best basketball. Last season, he struggled early, making just 14 of 46 shots over his first five games. I think it's a little too soon. ### 8. Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.8 credits, owned by 16.0%) This feels like a very straightforward pick. [Sylvain Francisco] was one of the best players in the 2025-26 EuroLeague, Kendrick Nunn is injured, and he's expected to take on a bigger role right away. A very solid choice. ### 7. Alec Peters, Olimpia Armani Milan (11.7 credits, owned by 17.2%) I understand why Fantasy managers are going for [Alec Peters]. He's an elite power forward at a very reasonable price, offers significant upside and is expected to enjoy an expanded role. Personally, I'd like to wait a little longer and see how quickly he adjusts to his new surroundings. ### 6. Ousmane Diop, Olimpia Armani Milan (4.0 credits, owned by 17.6%) Now this is a surprise. I hadn't even considered him. There are very few budget options at center this season, and [Ousmane Diop] is expected to get some minutes. My advice? Spend big on both center spots. It's one of the most important decisions Fantasy managers will make this year. ### 5. Jordan Nwora, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade (13.0 credits, owned by 17.6%) This is one of the names I expected to see. [Jordan Nwora] is a natural mismatch, right in the middle of his prime and playing for a coach whose style suits him perfectly. Let's just say he'll be in more than a few of my teams, and pretty often at that. ### 4. Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas (15.5 credits, owned by 25.8%) Probably the most important player in the game right now. If [Jonas Valanciunas] performs as expected, he'll be a double-double machine and an absolute must-have. As things stand, going without him feels very risky. He has a really high fantasy floor. ### 3. Arijan Lakic, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (4.0 credits, owned by 27.4%) I expected to see budget options this high on the list, but not [Arijan Lakic], to be honest. Yes, he should have a place in Partizan's rotation, but if you're shopping in this price range, I'd rather go with Stefan Joksimovic of Baskonia or Eleftherios Mantzoukas of Panathinaikos. ### 2. Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (13.6 credits, owned by 27.9%) One of my favorite guards in the game. It's difficult to choose [Carlik Jones] over Sylvain Francisco or TJ Shorts, but as the leader of his team with a home opener ahead of him, I completely understand this pick. He should deliver. ### 1. Sasha Vezenkov, Olympiacos Piraeus (17.0 credits, owned by 37.1%) [Sasha Vezenkov] bails you out. That's the bottom line. He rescues Fantasy managers from disaster, round after round. He's always there, whether you need a reliable captain in Round 1 or someone to save your score in Round 2. The Fantasy GOAT. Always has been. Maybe always will be.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Guards
text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] is just around the corner, and I have some good news for you. I'm expanding my coverage, and from now on, you'll get three fantasy tips articles every week -- one each for guards, [forwards] and [centers]. As always, I'll also revisit my previous recommendations and hold myself accountable for the good picks and the bad ones. Since it's Round 1, however, there's no need to look back yet. No mistakes to regret and no victories to celebrate. I'm starting with guards, and I've included players from a variety of price ranges to help every Fantasy Challenge manager. Here are five guards who deserve serious consideration before tipoff. ### TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket (14.9 credits) One official game was enough to show what [TJ Shorts] can do as the leader of a team whose style fits him perfectly. He finished with 17 points, 6 rebounds, 7 assists and a PIR of 29 against FC Barcelona in the Spanish Super Cup. The signs are already there. Expect a big season. ### Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.8 credits) This one feels like a no-brainer. [Sylvain Francisco] earned All-EuroLeague First Team honors with Zalgiris last season and now joins a team whose primary scoring guard, Kendrick Nunn, is sidelined. Panathinaikos will play seven of its first eight games at home, giving Francisco an excellent opportunity to start the season strongly. ### Nigel Williams-Goss, Zalgiris Kaunas (9.7 credits) With Francisco no longer in Kaunas, [Nigel Williams-Goss] is expected to take on greater offensive responsibility and spend more time with the ball in his hands. He enjoyed a strong preseason and posted a PIR of 15 in his first official game despite playing only 16 minutes. Fantasy managers should keep a close eye on him, as his role is set to grow. ### Matteo Spagnolo, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (6.4 credits) It's true that injuries and absences during the preseason helped create opportunities for [Matteo Spagnolo], but the potential is hard to ignore. At just 6.4 credits, few players offer his upside. He recorded 10 points and 8 rebounds in his first official game of the season while playing nearly 22 minutes. That's outstanding value. ### Mario Saint-Supery, Valencia Basket (4.7 credits) [Mario Saint-Supery] left the NCAA to take on a significant role with Valencia and immediately showed why. Against Barcelona, he played a little over 18 minutes and produced 6 points, 4 assists and a PIR of 10. He's creative, versatile and capable of scoring in different ways. At under 5 credits, he may be the biggest bargain among guards heading into Round 1.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Forwards
text: The 2026-27 EuroLeague season is here, and so is the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. The game returns to a single-stage format in which every game matters, just like on the court. This season, I'm expanding my coverage with three Fantasy tips articles every week, one for each position -- [guards], forwards and [centers]. And yes, I'll revisit my previous picks every week, so I'll have to live with my successes and mistakes, the same way I do every week as co-host of the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast. It's time to talk about forwards. I'll stay away from fantasy king Sasha Vezenkov of Olympiacos Piraeus for obvious reasons and focus instead on players across a range of price points who can help your team succeed. Here are five forwards I like, other than Sasha. ### Jordan Nwora, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade (13.0 credits) This is an easy pick. [Jordan Nwora] is coming off a breakout season and now has arguably even more talent around him. Under Ibon Navarro, whose teams thrive in an up-tempo system, he could take another step forward. If Zvezda wins enough games, don't be surprised to see Nwora competing for MVP of the Round honors and All-EuroLeague Team recognition. ### Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Real Madrid (12.8 credits) [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot] was arguably one of the most consistent Fantasy performers last season with Baskonia. He joins a bigger club, but his role should remain largely the same: finding open spaces, knocking down shots and contributing efficiently across the board. His game looks perfectly suited to coach Pedro Martinez's system. ### Joel Parra, FC Barcelona (7.0 credits) Barcelona added plenty of new faces during the summer, so it's reasonable to expect the team's established players to log more minutes early in the season. [Joel Parra] is coming off an excellent preseason in which he regularly posted double-digit PIR performances. His attractive price tag only adds to the appeal. He looks ready for a breakout year. ### Eleftherios Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (4.5 credits) This might be one of the biggest surprises of the preseason. With Nigel Hayes-Davis sidelined, many expected Dinos Mitoglou and Juancho Hernangomez to absorb most of the extra minutes. Instead, [Eleftherios Mantzoukas] has been given a real opportunity and made the most of it throughout the preseason. If his three-point shot continues to fall, his Fantasy value could rise quickly. ### Stefan Joksimovic, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (4.0 credits) It's time for EuroLeague fans to get acquainted with [Stefan Joksimovic], who has starred at youth level for both Baskonia and the Slovenian national team. He's a gifted scorer and an all-around contributor who appears set to earn minutes right away. At the minimum Fantasy price, he represents one of the most intriguing budget options available.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Centers
text: It's the start of the 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] season, and everyone starts from scratch. You have just as much chance to win the grand prize as any other manager. You just have to make the right choices. I'm here to help, and between running the game and co-hosting the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast, I watch this stuff obsessively. If I get it wrong, well, we can all laugh about it later. It's a fantasy game, after all. This season, I'll publish three Fantasy tips articles every week -- one for each position -- as I expand my coverage even further. You'll get five recommendations for [guards], [forwards] and centers. The rest is up to you. It's time to talk about centers, so let's dive in. ### Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas (15.5 credits) [Jonas Valanciunas] is back in the EuroLeague after what feels like an eternity away. In the meantime, he grabbed more than 9,000 rebounds in the NBA. He arrives in Kaunas as Zalgiris's main offensive threat and should be a double-double machine, much like Arvydas Sabonis was in the 2003-04 season. ### Moses Wright, EA7 Emporio Armani Milan (14.0 credits) [Moses Wright] had an impressive season with Zalgiris and now arrives in Milan with a major role waiting for him. Expect efficient scoring, even from long range, blocked shots and plenty of rebounds. It's hard to choose between Valanciunas and Wright, so if your budget allows it, why not take both? ### Austin Wiley, FC Bayern Munich (11.0 credits) If you're looking for a slightly more affordable center, [Austin Wiley] could be your guy. He's coming off a fantastic BKT EuroCup season with Hapoel Bank Yahav Jerusalem, finishing as the competition's leading rebounder while averaging just 21 minutes per game. Yes, this is the EuroLeague, but his PIR floor looks remarkably solid. ### Allan Dokossi, Paris Basketball (8.0 credits) [Allan Dokossi] had his ups and downs last season while splitting time between power forward and center, but this year could bring much greater consistency. He's an excellent rebounder, an energy player and someone who fills the stat sheet. His first official game offered plenty of encouragement: 14 points and a PIR of 24 in just 22 minutes. ### Kevarrius Hayes, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (7.3 credits) There aren't many budget-friendly options at center, and several low-cost picks may struggle for meaningful playing time. Partizan has excellent depth in the paint, but [Kevarrius Hayes] is an experienced player, an elite shot-blocker and a strong rebounder available at an affordable price. He should definitely be on your radar.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: 10 Best Tips
text: Preparations for the new season are in full swing, and Basketball Sphere is set to deliver the most comprehensive EuroLeague Fantasy coverage throughout the entire 2026/27 campaign. Our goal is to provide you with all the data and insights needed to build a championship-caliber team and make smart decisions round after round. Alongside our team-by-team breakdowns, each day will bring a new dedicated topic to keep you ahead of the competition. We will systematically cover every critical angle for your draft and weekly lineups. Through these deep dives, you will gain key insights into coaching tactics and rotation roles – the crucial factors that drive Fantasy output. The EuroLeague is about to begin, and so is our favorite game, EuroLeague Fantasy. If you want to stay one step ahead of the competition, it’s not enough to simply pick the best players. Good results often come down to the details and players flying under the radar whom others fail to identify in time. That’s why we’ve put together 10 fantasy tips that could take your game to the next level. EuroLeague Fantasy Basketball Sphere Competiton: JOIN the Challenge and Win Prizes 1. Pick players for multiple rounds Analyzing fixture difficulty is critical for long-term fantasy success . Before acquiring a player, evaluate their team’s upcoming schedule over the next three to four rounds. Identifying a target with a favorable sequence of games creates a durable asset for your roster. This forward-looking approach minimizes the need for frequent transfers, preserving flexibility for future rounds. Consequently, you can conserve valuable trade resources and concentrate on optimizing weaker positions across the rest of your squad. Plan ahead to build a stable lineup and maximize total fantasy production. 2. Don’t save credits on coaches Invest heavily in your head coach rather than saving credits. Premium options around 10 credits offer exceptional value, frequently securing a dependable 20 points when facing favorable matchups. Replicating that production with a 10-credit player is extremely rare. Apply schedule analysis to coaches just as you would with players. A premium coach with a soft stretch of games over multiple rounds serves as a stable scoring anchor. Keeping a reliable coach long term eliminates unnecessary transfers, allowing you to reallocate those valuable trade resources toward upgrading other positions across your roster. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: The Best Rookies 3. Have a backup captain for the second day Selecting your captain is a critical decision, as their performance earns double points. Design your roster with two premium captain options split across the schedule: one competing on the first day and another on the second. If your initial captain delivers a disappointing score, having a top-tier alternative on day two provides vital insurance. This setup allows you to switch the armband and take a second shot at high output. Structuring your squad around split-day captains mitigates risk and ensures a dependable fallback to maximize your total round score. 4. Have a backup center for the second day The center position in EuroLeague Fantasy is unique because we can select only two centers, unlike guards and forwards, where we choose four players. Centers very often produce the highest number of fantasy points. The advice is to try to have one center playing on the first day and another on the second day, as the second day center gives us another chance to make up for a poor performance, just like with the captain. If we have to use both centers on the first day, our advice is to use the two-center formation, because it can happen that a cheaper center scores more points than the more expensive one . In that case, we would have no opportunity to make a substitution between the first and second day. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Will Have Smaller Roles Compared to Their Previous Teams 5. Pick players from weaker teams Targeting standout performers from bottom-tier teams separates elite fantasy managers from average ones. Most competitors overlook these rosters entirely, yet key players on weaker squads carry high usage rates and generate massive fantasy output. Avoid deploying them against elite defensive teams. Instead, target them when bottom-table sides face off in competitive, high-possession matchups. In these balanced contests, first options on weaker teams shoulder the entire offensive load, transforming into high-value, must-have assets. Exploiting these lower-profile fixtures provides a distinct competitive edge and unlocks massive scoring potential for your roster. 6. Focus on making profit at the start Prioritize team value accumulation over short-term point tallies during the opening weeks. Your main objective across the first 10 rounds is expanding your credit budget by targeting undervalued assets capable of far exceeding their price tags. Building a high-value roster early yields massive long-term dividends. A inflated credit pool provides maximum flexibility, allowing you to easily afford premium superstars and elite options later in the season. Focus on roster appreciation early to set a strong financial foundation, expanding your budget and unlocking far greater flexibility for the rest of the campaign. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Produce Well but Aren’t Fantasy Options 7. Avoid players priced between 4.2 and 5.0 credits This is a tip that does not necessarily have to apply all the time, but it is particularly relevant at the very start of the season. We believe players in this price range should generally be avoided because they usually have very limited minutes, which means they don’t have enough time to produce a solid fantasy performance. This can lead to small losses in team value, which can add up significantly if the same mistake is repeated round after round. If a serious fantasy option appears in this price range, of course he should be considered, but our advice at the beginning is to go for 4.0-credit players instead. They cannot decrease our team value, and they might even make us some credits. There are a few interesting 4.0-credit options this season. 8. Avoid players from low-scoring games Another rule that many fantasy players overlook is the expected scoring level of a game. Players from teams that traditionally play at a high pace and score a lot of points are excellent fantasy options, and above all, so are their opponents. On the other hand, tougher teams that play in low-scoring games are worth avoiding, because fewer points in a game generally means fewer fantasy points for the players involved, and vice versa: more points in a game usually means more fantasy points for the players in that game. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Veterans Who Can Still Be Leaders 9. Follow the injury report Monitoring injury reports is essential for uncovering high-value fantasy opportunities. When a key player is sidelined, their absence frees up substantial court time and usage for remaining teammates. A backup center, guard, or forward stepping into a starting role instantly becomes a potent target. Combine roster shortages with favorable matchups. If an elevated backup faces an opponent that struggles to defend their position, they transform into a mandatory pick. Tracking injuries allows you to capitalize on temporary usage spikes, secure premium production at lower costs, and gain a decisive edge over managers who react too late. 10. Be patient and don’t react impulsively If we bring in a player for the next three rounds and he has a poor performance in the first round, we should never sell him immediately after a bad game. We need to be patient and stick with him until the end of the planned period. Very often, a player will have a fantastic game in the following round, and if we have sold him, we will be left regretting the decision. At the same time, we should avoid playing impulsively. title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips Round 1
text: As I always did, I’m just going to ignore some of the obvious expensive options like Sasa Vezenkov, Jonas Valanciunas, Sylvain Francisco, Mike James, etc. I always like to include those players who are not that obvious or if they are, at least in the moment I recommend them is one of the best moments of the season, based on matchup streak, current shape, etc. 🧠GUARDS TJ Shorts (14.9 cr): He’s a expensive, yet obvious choice in guard position, I know. However, I include him just because I think he’s the best guard option on the game this season, as he managed to land on a team where can be the real TJ we’ve seen in Paris or Bonn. A player that has a main role, the ball is on his hands most of the time, so he can decide what to do on almost each offensive play. Points and assists will never be lacking from him, so I think he’s also a safe bet, as he’ll be quite consistent. Carlik Jones (13.6 cr): Similar reasons to the ones I mentioned for TJ. He’ll have a mian role on a team where he’s the clear leader in terms of playmaking and scoring. He has a good relationship with the fans and coach Peñarroya, so he’ll be high on confidence and will be used a lot in EuroLeague, so perfect mix. Vasilije Micic (12 cr): His preseason has been quite brutal, averaging 21 PIR in 4 games played. That makes me think he could be again on full confidence and we could see the MVP version of Micic on a team that has a long guard rotation, but needs a player like him to work really well. I know it’s a risk cause last season he was terrible, but I can see another face on Vasilije this season. Trent Forrest (10.6 cr): One of the most complete players, with a crazy ability to take profit from each and every minute he’s on the court. In terms of FPTS/min he’s one of the best choices, so knowing that Saras loves players like him, he could have a really outstanding season in terms of efficiency. The only risk is the scoring side, cause there are games where he just focus on the playmaking area and takes few shots. Iffe Lundberg (8.3 cr): A really complete combo guard who can contribute from every aspect of the game, so that makes him a great choice. He’ll have a big usage with Kattash, but don’t expect massive performances from him, as he’s strength is his consistency on good performances, but most of them around 10-20 FPTS. He will play in Turn 2 of Round 2, so he’s a great pick thinking for both rounds at the same time. Matteo Spagnolo (6.4 cr): Amazing preseason being one of the leaders of this short Baskonia roster and having the trust of coach Galbiati on him. He’s a full package player, as he’s really good rebounding and assisting, but sometimes also on the scoring side, which makes him a great steal on low-priced players. I could also add some interesting names like Mario Saint-Supéry (4.7) , Andrés Feliz (6.2) , Leandro Bolmaro (8.7), Tremont Waters (9.9), Matthew Strazel (10.3) or Horton-Tucker (12.7). 🎯FORWARDS Jordan Nwora (13 cr): Might be on his best moment since landing in Europe, as he’s confidence and efficiency on the scoring side is mindblowing, averaging 17.8 pts in 5 games. He also has a really great capacity to rebound, so that makes him a really good choice for a high-usage player that in my opinion is really underpriced right now. Nikola Mirotic (11.6 cr): One of the most notable players in Europe this last decade and one of the most Fantasy-friendly players ever, as he drawns a massive amount of fouls by game, he has an outstanding rebounding capacity and on the scoring side no doubt that he’s one of the best PF on the league. I think 11.6 is not his real price and his ceiling is way higher, even more on a roster like the Valencia one. Bonzie Colson (11.3 cr): His preseason has been excellent, showing that he’s the main SF on rotation and that he’s on a really great moment on his career in terms of scoring, but also on the rebounding side. He averaged 14.8 PIR in 5 games grabbing 4.2 reb and scoring 15.2 ppg, which are really correct numbers. Eugene Omoruyi (10.5 cr): Even though his preseason has not been the best in the end, he started in a really great way, showing that he’ll be the main PF for coach Alimpijevic, especially in EuroLeague. Last season he showed his efficiency on court with Baskonia and this season in Besiktas he’ll have a similar role, so this is my risky bid for the start of the season. Braxton Key (8 cr): What a SuperCup for him and preseason overall too, showing one of the most complete versions of himself. He comes after a massive end of season with Valencia leading that playoff serie against Pao and now he faces a new season on a team where the rotation is bigger, but he might take a main role and be really efficient. Joel Parra (7 cr): Now we’re in front of the best Forward option right now. A player that last season already showed his quality, but he started this season unbelievably well. His confidence to take the important shots, no regrets on 3pt shooting, the energy on defense and offensive rebounding, the ability to take the ball out and bring some assists, etc. Everything is looking well on him this start of the season. I would add Azuolas Tubelis (11.1) , Kessler Edwards (10), Miles Norris (8.9) , Lamar Stevens (8), Tyson Ward (7.5) & Dinos Mitoglou (5.5). 🗼CENTERS Moses Wright (14 cr): The must on this center position, as he has been the best player during this preseason, he comes after a massive breakout season in Zalgiris and in my opinion, he’s the most dominant center in Europe right now. He will be used a lot as he’s the main center and has really great playmakers to feed even more his scoring quality under the basket. Donta Hall (10.9 cr): Even if Milutinov is ready to play on this opening round of the season, Hall is on a level right now that’s pretty crazy. He does not need to play a lot, to get massive efficiency performances like the ones he did on this preseason averaging 18.2 PIR per game. So if Milu is out, he’s a must, if Milu can play, he remains a great option on this price range. Bruno Fernando (10.3 cr): Finally having the main role he wanted in Europe, accompanied by 2 of the best playmakers in the league, makes him one of the best options. He’s a really powerful center with a great rebounding capacity and improving day by day his scoring efficiency on the paint. He will have a high-usage with Laso, so I think you should all consider him for your teams. Nikola Tanaskovic (7.8 cr): A big sleeper in my opinion, as he comes after a really great season in EuroCup with Buducnost and as we saw in this preseason, he will have the trust of coach Peñarroya. He’s a player that really takes advantage from each and every minute that he’s on the court, so on that price, he could deliver really great performances. Thanks for reading EuroBallin' Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Round 1 Tips: Best Player Picks & Head Coaches
text: Preparations for the new season are in full swing, and Basketball Sphere is set to deliver the most comprehensive EuroLeague Fantasy coverage throughout the entire 2026/27 campaign. Our goal is to provide you with all the data and insights needed to build a championship-caliber team and make smart decisions round after round. EuroLeague Fantasy Basketball Sphere Competiton: JOIN the Challenge and Win Prizes With the EuroLeague season just around the corner and games tipping off this Thursday, we’ve put together our top Fantasy picks for Round 1 across all three positions. Whether you’re looking for premium stars, solid mid-level producers, or budget-friendly value players, these picks will help you build the perfect roster to start the season strong. Guards Best options over 10.0 credits Elijah Bryant – Hapoel Tel Aviv – 15.5 credits Elijah Bryant enters the season as the clear leading star for Hapoel Tel Aviv , positioned to pick up right where he left off during his dominant previous campaign. Hapoel Tel Aviv opens their EuroLeague run against Bayern , a match-up where Bryant should exploit clear defensive mismatches opposite Andreas Obst . Given full starter minutes, he possesses immense upside and stands as a strong candidate to clear 25 fantasy points in Round 1. Sylvain Francisco – Panathinaikos – 14.8 credits Panathinaikos enters the opening stretch of the EuroLeague season with an exceptionally favorable schedule, making their core contributors essential targets for Fantasy rosters. With Kendrick Nunn sidelined by injury, Sylvain Francisco is primed to step up and direct the Greek side’s backcourt rotation. Factoring in the high-tempo matchup against Paris and his expanded role, Francisco projects to log around 30 minutes on court, giving him clear upside to comfortably surpass the 20 fantasy point threshold in Round 1. Carlik Jones – Partizan – 13.6 credits Carlik Jones enters the new EuroLeague season as the clear focal point of Partizan’s attack, expected to handle the bulk of primary creation responsibilities. Partizan enjoys a very manageable schedule over the opening three rounds, giving them a solid runway to build early momentum. However, their overall offensive efficiency will heavily rely on Jones producing at an elite, high-usage level. Opening Round 1 at home against Milano, expect Jones to be fully motivated to put on a dominant show in front of the Belgrade crowd, making him a prime fantasy pick. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: The Best Rookies Best options from 6.0 to 10.0 credits David DeJulius – Besiktas – 9.9 credits Besiktas opens their campaign against Valencia, giving David DeJulius a clear physical edge in his primary matchup. Standing roughly 10 cm taller than Valencia’s T.J. Shorts , DeJulius should be able to leverage his size advantage to consistently force mismatches, collapse defenses, and generate quality scoring looks. Given his role as a creator, if he manages to post a PIR around 15, he will firmly solidify himself as a high-value budget option for Round 1. Yam Madar – Maccabi Tel Aviv – 8.8 credits Maccabi Tel Aviv kicks off their EuroLeague campaign against Asvel, a side that has consistently ranked near the bottom of the standings in recent seasons. Yam Madar , after underwhelming stint at Hapoel Tel Aviv, is stepping into a bigger role at Maccabi Tel Aviv, positioning himself as one of the team’s leaders, particularly in backcourt. Given the favorable matchup and his growing responsibilities in controlling the game’s rhythm, Madar should have plenty of freedom to operate, make a strong impact, and deliver solid fantasy returns in Round 1. Best options under 6.0 credits Juan Nunez – Barcelona – 4.6 credits With reliable, budget-friendly backcourt targets scarce in this price tier, Barcelona point guard Juan Nunez stands out as an intriguing punt for Round 1. Priced at just 4.6 credits, Nunez offers real value for managers needing to free up capital. If he earns around 10 minutes of action in the rotation, he possesses the playmaking talent to carve out a 5–10 PIR return. While head coach Aleksander Sekulic’s backcourt rotation remains uncertain entering the opening week, Nunez carries enough upside to warrant consideration as a low-risk fill-in. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Will Have Smaller Roles Compared to Their Previous Teams Forwards Best options over 10.0 credits Sasha Vezenkov – Olympiacos – 17.0 credits Sasha Vezenkov stands as the undisputed king of EuroLeague Fantasy. Leaving him out of your Round 1 squad feels like an unnecessary gamble given his unmatched consistency and elite floor. Olympiacos opens their campaign on the road against Baskonia in what projects to be a high-scoring, up-tempo clash. In this exact fixture during their previous opening-day meeting, Vezenkov dominated the floor with a massive 24-point, 13-rebound double-double. Expect him to put up another dominant stat line and deliver captain-worthy fantasy output right out of the gate. Guerschon Yabusele – Panathinaikos – 14.3 credits As noted, Panathinaikos players represent essential pick-ups for the start of the EuroLeague campaign, making Guerschon Yabusele a standout option for Round 1. With both Moustapha Fall and Nigel Hayes-Davis sidelined by injuries, the frontcourt rotation for the Greek giants has thinned out considerably. As a result, Yabusele should absorb heavy usage across both the power forward and center. This expanded role grants him clear upside and high minutes, positioning him to deliver premium fantasy value right away. Eugene Omoruyi – Besiktas – 10.5 credits Besiktas hosts Valencia in the opening EuroLeague round, and alongside DeJulius, Eugene Omoruyi stands out as a strong pick. A major reason to target two Besiktas players is scheduling: Round 2 features only two games on its second day, with Besiktas slated to play in that light slate. Paired with their overall favorable early-season schedule, owning at least one of these core contributors is essential to optimize your squad’s flexibility and roster coverage. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Produce Well but Aren’t Fantasy Options Best options from 6.0 to 10.0 credits Lamar Stevens – Partizan – 8.0 credits Partizan hosts Milano in the EuroLeague opening round, where Lamar Stevens emerges as a sneaky, budget-friendly option. With Partizan’s forward rotation looking thin entering the season , Stevens has a clear runway to carve out immediate fantasy value at a modest 8.0 credits. Expect him to log around 25 minutes in this matchup, giving him plenty of court time to make an impact through his scoring, defense, and high-activity play. Joel Parra – Barcelona – 7.0 credits Joel Parra represents arguably the biggest fantasy steal in the EuroLeague right now . Throughout the preseason, he stepped up alongside Kevin Punter to establish himself as one of Barcelona’s main focal points on offense. A price tag of just 7.0 credits is exceptionally low for a player stepping into such a expanded role and holding this much raw upside. He stands out as an essential long-term hold for your squad, as his low entry cost gives him massive potential for a substantial credit price increase as the season unfolds. Best options under 6.0 credits Stefan Joksimovic – Baskonia – 4.0 credits Young Slovenian prospect Stefan Joksimovic serves as a low-risk punt for the opening round at this extreme budget level. Given his minimal price, even a quiet outing carries virtually no drawback, protecting your squad from negative fantasy valuation early on. Should Olympiacos build an early lead and pull away from Baskonia , garbage time could open up extended minutes for Joksimovic, giving him surprising upside to chip in unexpected box-score stats. title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 1: Thursday
text: Opening night of the 2026-27 EuroLeague season is in the books and Thursday's slate of games already delivered its share of heroes and heartbreak – especially for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers. Whether you're basking in the glow of a breakout performance from a value pick or nursing the wounds of a big-money bust who no-showed, every fantasy manager has a story to tell after night one. Let's break down which players padded your scoreline and which ones left you searching for the bench button. Here are Thursday’s fantasy winners and losers: ### Fantasy winners #### [Tyler Dorsey, Olympiacos Piraeus] Last season, Dorsey scored at least 20 points in his first two games. He started strong again this season with 25 points on excellent shooting to finish with 31.9 fantasy points. Though Dorsey is not a cheap player, coming in at 12.6 credits, he provided plenty of value to the 3.5% of owners who signed him for Round 1. #### [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne] Still a teenager, Fodzo Dada posted a manly performance for ASVEL at home with 14 points and 5 assists for 18.7 fantasy points, which cost a mere 4.8 credits! I recommended him on the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast], but what can I do that only 1.1% of owners took my advice? I am pretty sure that number will rise this week, but you will be buying him at a higher price. #### [Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas] While all the attention was on his frontcourt mate [Jonas Valanciunas], Tubelis was almost as productive, but at a significant discount. The Zalgiris power forward posted 10 points and a career-high 12 rebounds, recording his second EuroLeague double-double, while totaling 25.3 fantasy points. That’s quite a haul for his 11.1-credit price tag. Tubelis was owned by 6.5% of fantasy owners, and those managers were winners on Thursday, too. ### Fantasy losers #### [Johnathan Motley, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] Center is not always an easy fantasy position. And if you were among the 2.5% of fantasy owners who had Motley in your lineup, it became a nightmare position for you on Thursday. One in 40 fantasy teams spent 11.0 credits on a center who recorded minus-13 fantasy points. Ouch! Even though in almost all cases Motley will wind up on the fantasy bench (every owner who has a pulse and a phone will bench him on Friday), which will mitigate the damage, this performance will also result in lost credits. Ouch again! #### [Nikola Milutinov, Olympiacos Piraeus] I don’t know why, but 2.6% of fantasy owners had Milutinov this week despite the injury concerns. In the end, he played 9 minutes off the bench and scored 3.3 fantasy points. His owners paid 15.3 credits for that. Milutinov was the sixth-highest priced player in the game and will be among the lowest-scoring fantasy players in Round 1. From a credit standpoint, it would have been better for his owners had Milutinov not played at all. #### [Joel Parra, FC Barcelona] This one hurt a lot of fantasy players because Parra is the second-most-owned player in Round 1 at a whopping 30.9%! Parra started and played nearly 27 minutes, which is great for a player who cost 7.0 credits. However, on Thursday he shot poorly, missing 8 of the 10 shots he took. That left him with a fantasy score of 0. Well, at least his owners have plenty of company.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 1: Friday
text: - [Thursday's Fantasy Challenge winners and losers] Only three games were played on Friday, but for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers, there was still plenty to watch. The best was saved for last, at least for some. Here are my Fantasy Challenge winners and losers from Night 2 of Round 1. ### Fantasy winners ##### Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade Hats off to the 27.5% of you who had [Carlik Jones] on your fantasy team. The Partizan star went for 36.3 fantasy points on a 20-point, 10-assist night, boosting his price from 13.6 to 14.5 credits. He could be this season's must-have fantasy player. ##### Braxton Key, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul The 16.4% of managers who had [Braxton Key] knew what they were doing: 24.2 fantasy points. His 8.0-credit price already looks like a steal given his importance to Fenerbahce, and despite the +0.6 rise, Key looks like a lock in coach Sarunas Jasikevicius's rotation. ##### TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket For those who had faith in [TJ Shorts] at a new team, well done. Only 11.7% of managers had him, which surprised me given how good he was in fantasy at Paris Basketball in 2024-25. He finished his Valencia debut with 22.0 fantasy points, looking like that version again. His price already jumped to from 14.9 to 15.1 credits, and expect that number to keep climbing. ### Fantasy losers ##### Moses Wright, Armani Olimpia Milan This is the pick that hurt the most people. Nearly one in five managers (19.3%) had [Moses Wright], and 9.0 fantasy points fell well short after his form in the Italian Super Cup. At 14.0 credits, he was already an expensive bet, and Friday cost him another -0.3, dropping him to 13.7. Still, I'd expect him to bounce back in Tuesday's Italian derby. ##### RJ Cole, Armani Olimpia Milan [RJ Cole]'s competition debut at Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade was a night to forget: -6 fantasy points, and his price dropped from 8.5 to 7.9 credits. Only 0.3% of managers owned him, but spare a thought for them. I wouldn't read too much into one rough night on the road for a rookie. It's only up from here. ##### Rasheed Bello, Virtus Bologna Another newcomer with a tricky start. Just 0.2% of managers had [Rasheed Bello], and he finished with -4 fantasy points as his price fell from 11.0 to 10.4 credits. That was already steep for a newcomer, so it's worth watching whether managers hold out for a bounce-back or jump ship.

title: Super Cup: Η «Χρυσή Βίβλος» των νικητών του θεσμού!
text: Ο Ολυμπιακός επικράτησε του ΠΑΟΚ με 101-96 για τον τελικό του Super Cup . Οι «ερυθρόλευκοι» είναι η ομάδα με τις περισσότερες κατακτήσεις , ενώ η φετινή, ήταν η πέμπτη συνεχόμενη φορά που κερδίζουν τον θεσμό . title: Βεζένκοφ: «Κατακτήσαμε τον πιο μικρό στόχο της σεζόν, έχουμε άλλους τρεις»! (video)
text: Ο Ολυμπιακός επικράτησε του ΠΑΟΚ στο Περιστέρι (101-96), και κατέκτησε τον πρώτο φετινό του τίτλο και το πέμπτο ελληνικό Super Cup στην ιστορία του. Μετά το φινάλε της αναμέτρησης ο MVP του Ολυμπιακού , Σάσα Βεζένκοφ , δήλωσε στον ΣΚΑΪ : Ολυμπιακός: Κυρίαρχος και αήττητος σε Super Cup! «Κατακτήσαμε τον πιο μικρό στόχο της σεζόν, έχουμε άλλους τρεις. Το πιο σημαντικό είναι να βελτιωθούμε. Το ελληνικό μπάσκετ ανεβαίνει, να έχουμε υγεία και εμείς και όλες οι ομάδες και να έχουμε ένα καλό πρωτάθλημα».

text: Του Μιχάλη Γκιουλένογλου/ info@eurohoops.net Ο Ολυμπιακός ήταν ο νικητής του Stoiximan Super Cup 2026 , μετά την επικράτηση επί του ΠΑΟΚ με 101-96, στο κλειστό του Περιστερίου. title: Ολυμπιακός - ΠΑΟΚ: Τα highlights του τελικού του Super Cup
text: Δείτε τις καλύτερες στιγμές της επικράτησης του Ολυμπιακού κόντρα στον ΠΑΟΚ στον τελικό του Super Cup.

title: Ο Παναθηναϊκός «ανέβασε» το φάουλ του Καλάθη και σχολίασε τη διαιτησία του τελικού: «Σαν να μην πέρασε μια μέρα»
text: Η ΚΑΕ Παναθηναϊκός AKTOR με σχετική ανάρτηση στάθηκε στην τελευταία φάση για την οποία διαμαρτυρήθηκε έντονα ο ΠΑΟΚ.

title: Τρινκιέρι σε δημοσιογράφο: «Ήσουν καλύτερη από μένα!»
text: Διαβάστε όσα είπε ο Αντρέα Τρινκιέρι στη συνέντευξη Τύπου μετά την ήττα του ΠΑΟΚ από τον Ολυμπιακό στον τελικό του Super Cup.

title: Άλλος τον τίτλο, άλλος τις εντυπώσεις!
text: Ο Ολυμπιακός κατέκτησε το Super Cup (101-96) στο κλειστό «Ανδρέας Παπανδρέου», αλλά ο ΠΑΟΚ ήταν αυτός που πήρε τα εύσημα.

title: Ολυμπιακός - ΠΑΟΚ: Οι αντιδράσεις του Γιαννακόπουλου για την έκβαση του τελικού
text: Ο Δημήτρης Γιαννακόπουλος μέσω Instagram story τοποθετήθηκε για τα όσα διαδραματίστηκαν στον τελικό του Super Cup ανάμεσα σε Ολυμπιακό και ΠΑΟΚ.

title: Βεζένκοβ: «Όταν δίνεις δικαίωμα στον ΠΑΟΚ να γυρίσει ρισκάρεις»
text: Ο Σάσα Βεζένκοβ έκανε το δικό του σχόλιο μετά τη νίκη του Ολυμπιακού επί του ΠΑΟΚ και την κατάκτηση του Σούπερ Καπ.

title: Ρεάλ - Μάλαγα 89-87: Οι Μαδριλένοι πήραν το θρίλερ με την Ουνικάχα
text: Η Ρεάλ πήρε δια πυρός και σιδήρου τη νίκη απέναντι στην Ουνικάχα Μάλαγα με 89-87 και άνοιξε... λογαριασμό στο φετινό πρωτάθλημα της ACB.

title: Όσμαν: «Είμαι περήφανος για την ομάδα μου, είδα ότι δεν θα έπαιρνα τα σφυρίγματα που έπρεπε απόψε»
text: Ο Τσέντι Όσμαν παραχώρησε δηλώσεις μετά το τέλος του τελικού του Super Cup με τον Ολυμπιακό, όπου ο ΠΑΟΚ ηττήθηκε με 101-96. Ο Τούρκος παίκτης δήλωσε περήφανος για την προσπάθεια της ομάδας του.

title: Αναντολού Εφές - Μπεσίκτας 95-81: Πρεμιέρα με εμφατική νίκη για την ομάδα του Λάσο
text: Η Αναντολού Εφές μπήκε με το δεξί στο τουρκικό πρωτάθλημα, επικρατώντας της Μπεσίκτας με 95-81 και δείχνοντας από νωρίς τις διαθέσεις της.

title: Σολέ - Βιλερμπάν 85-97: Πέταγε φωτιές πριν το παιχνίδι με τον Παναθηναϊκό
text: Η Βιλερμπάν δεν είχε κανένα πρόβλημα να επικρατήσει της Σολέ εκτός έδρας με 97-85 και να ξεκινήσει με το... δεξί τις υποχρεώσεις της στο γαλλικό πρωτάθλημα.

title: Παναθηναϊκός: «ΜΠΡΑΒΟ ΕΛΛΑΔΑΡΑ»
text: Η ΚΑΕ Παναθηναϊκός AKTOR έστειλε τα δικά της συγχαρητήρια στην Εθνική Ομάδα Ποδοσφαίρου για την μεγάλη της νίκη μέσα στην Γερμανία.

title: Ολυμπιακός: Το άριστο πρώτο ημίχρονο και η υπογραφή των σταρ
text: Ο Παναγιώτης Ραμαντάνης γράφει για την εικόνα του Ολυμπιακού στον τελικό του Σούπερ Καπ και την κατάκτηση του πρώτου τίτλου της σεζόν.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips Round 2 & 3
text: As I always did, I’m just going to ignore some of the obvious expensive options like Sasa Vezenkov, Jonas Valanciunas, Sylvain Francisco, Mike James, etc. Round 2 has a particularity, cause only 4 teams will have their matchup in Turn 2, so that means we have to think about players to captain in those 4 teams, to be able to have a decent captain in both turns. I always like to include those players who are not that obvious or if they are, at least in the moment I recommend them is one of the best moments of the season, based on matchup streak, current shape, etc. I also tend to not repeat the ones I recommended last round, so take all this into account. 🧠GUARDS Chris Jones (12.6 cr): On the roster analysis for Zvezda I already talked about him possibly nearing his prime on this Zvezda, and I was not far from the truth. He has started the season in a really great way, showing leadership as playmaker, but also confience on the scoring side. He might not be the one with the biggest usage, but I think that will increase gradually. Theo Maledon (10 cr): We predicted Theo being one of the players taking a step forward with Pedro Martínez and that’s what we’ve seen until now. He did an amazing preseason, now he has started the season in an unbeatable way, being the best player in both games played so far (EL & ACB). Devon Hall (8.5 cr): We’ve already seen the usage coach Poetta will give him, so that added to his capacity to contribute from every aspect of the game, makes him a great option. He might not be the best scorer, but I think he’s a pretty safe player, as he probably won’t get a -5 FPTS game. Maodo Lo (7.1 cr): After finding out the 2-weeks injury of Nigel Williams-Goss, the first direct replacement that comes to my mind is Maodo Lo, who should be the one to get his minutes. He might not be on his best career moment, but he has the quality and talent to put up a really great performance as playmaker. Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada (5.3 cr): He seemed to have a really quick adaptation to top-level basketball and a pretty decent usage to be that young, so it looks like a great option on that price. He’ll play in Turn 2, so that makes it even better as a Round 2 choice, even though teammates like Patty Mills could be the musts. 🎯FORWARDS Kameron Taylor (12.6 cr): His last season was really good, but he started this one even better, so I think on a team where he might be one of the scoring references during all the season and with his rebounding capacity, the ceiling is really far from where he’s right now. Alec Peters (12 cr): While Garrison Mathews remains sidelined, he might be one of the best Forwards available in Fantasy terms. His playing time is already pretty high (30 mins) and will keep being like this as long as Mathews is injured. He just need to contribute a little bit more in rebounding and defensively to become the ultimate choice. Kessler Edwards (10 cr): He’s a really complete PF that already got a massive performance on this season Italian Supercup vs Milano (25 EFF). He can get +10 FPTS without even scoring, so imagine the potential if he gets a great game in terms of scoring, on a game that will be easier for him than Fener. Dinos Mitoglou (5.9 cr): He started the season in a really great shape, with the confidence he was missing last season, so being that cheap and while NHD keeps sidelined, he could have really great performances as he’s good on rebounding, but also on mid-range and 3pt shooting. 🗼CENTERS Mathias Lessort (15 cr): He’s an obvious choice, but especially this round against ASVEL and being probably the best captain option for Round 2, Turn 2. He seems to be again nearing his prime and that means the ceiling of this guy is still really far from 15 credits, so it might be time to select him. O. Balcerowski (8.3 cr) : As Nebo keeps sidelined, he’s performing on surprising numbers in both EuroLeague & ACB first games, so he might be one of the best mid-price centers right now. Great rebounding capacity and accompanied by pretty good playmakers in terms of creating spaces for him to end up alone under the basket. Jasiel Rivero (7.5 cr): Two great rounds ahead for Valencia facing 2 of the “weakest” teams on paper and especially Baskonia being a really bad frontcourt defender. That makes Jasiel a really good option to consider in cheap options, as he could be in advantage under the basket quite a lot of times. Thanks for reading EuroBallin' Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

text: Round 1 of the 2026-27 EuroLeague seasons is in the books and with it the first round of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge], too. Now we are heading into the first double-round week of the season. It is time to check the schedule, look for Turn 2 players who will deliver in Round 2, and reload your rosters before the next deadline, on Tuesday at 18:00 CET. My Round 1 picks were pretty good and three of them gained 0.2 credits! They were, TJ Shorts, who scored 22 fantasy points, Nigel Williams-Goss with 15.4 points and young Mario Saint-Supery with 11 fantasy points. Meanwhile Sylvain Francisco had 19.8 fantasy points and went up 0.1 credits. Alas, Matteo Spagnolo accounted for 7 fantasy points and his price remained the same. Here are five guards who deserve serious consideration for Round 2. I have made my picks at [forward] and [center], too. ### Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.9 credits) I said we would focus on T2 players, which means there will be a lot of Panathinaikos players in all fantasy articles this week. Panathinaikos is the heavy favorite to win both games at Telekom Center Athens. [Sylvain Francisco] signed for ASVEL early in the off-season and ended up playing for Panathinaikos. It should be a special game for him, so keep an eye on him. ### Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (14.5 credits) This is almost a no-brainer. [Carlik Jones] was the Round 1 MVP and even though Partizan plays twice on the road this week, it faces fast-paced teams in Paris and Bayern. He should keep leading Partizan the way he did in Round 1, making Jones a must for all fantasy teams. If you got him in Round 1, don't sell him. If you missed him, he is still affordable, so go for it. ### Scottie Wilbekin, Besiktas Istanbul (7.7 credits) In recent years, [Scottie Wilbekin] may not have been the best fantasy player, but at 7.7 credits, it is hard to ignore a player of his caliber. He had a solid Round 1 game against Valencia, getting a PIR of 13, and goes against Maccabi in Round 2. Wilbekin remains Maccabi's all-time top scorer in the EuroLeague with 1,801 points. Talent and motivation always go well together! ### Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne (5.3 credits) This is a surprise that few saw coming. [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada] took over in Round 1, leading ASVEL to an 84-74 home win over Maccabi with 14 points, 5 assists and a PIR of 17 as a starter, playing over 21 minutes. An isolated good game? Think again. Fodzo Dada also played almost 21 minutes in French League action, too. All aboard the Fodzo Dada train! ### Dovydas Giedraitis, Zalgiris Kaunas (4.3 credits) Owned by just 1.3% of fantasy managers at the moment, [Dovydas Giedraitis] is a very cheap option that should allow you to afford other players. [Nigel Williams-Goss] is sidelined for Zalgiris, which opens the door for Giedraitis, who started and played 20 minutes in the Lithuanian League on Sunday. Giedraitis is a cheap get for all fantasy managers.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Forwards
text: The 2026-27 EuroLeague is underway and so is the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. I know, Round 1 left some disappointments but now, you have four trades to improve your team. Even better, I are here to help you with some fantasy tips. MY picks at forward were disappointing for me too. Though I did well to recommend Eleftherios Mantzoukas of Panathinaikos, that's where the success ended. Mantzoukas scored 13.2 fantasy points and gained 0.3 credits. Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot (5 fantasy points, lost 0.4 credits), Joel Parra (0 fantasy points, lost 0.3 credits) and Jordan Nwora (8 fantasy points, lost 0.2 credits) all hurt their owners and the only reasons that Stefan Joksimovic (-1 fantasy points) didn’t lose credits is because he started at the minimum price. Yikes! I am determined to do better in all my picks this time. My recommendations at [guard] and [center] are already live and here are five forwards for the future for all budgets. ### Dario Saric, Anadolu Efes Istanbul (14.9 credits) That is the way you come back to the EuroLeague, with a huge game and leaving no doubt about your ability. [Dario Saric] had a strong Round 1 game against Barca with 17 points on 8-of-9 free throw shooting, 5 rebounds and 7 fouls drawn for a PIR of 26. He was also great in his team's Turkish League opener with 16 points and a PIR of 25. Real is up next, so expect him to keep leading Efes. ### Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas (11.6 credits) Frankie Sachs always talks about sensational sophomores in the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge podcast. [Azuolas Tubelis] had an outstanding first season and is determined to do even better now. He proved it in Round 1 against Zvezda with 10 points, 12 rebounds, 4 assists and a PIR of 23. At just 11.6 credits, Tubelis is a great opportunity for all fantasy managers out there. ### Tadas Sedekerskis, Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (10.5 credits) After an injury-plagued year, [Tadas Sedekerskis] is back and seems to be in good shape, too. He showed that against Olympiacos with 15 points and a PIR of 14 in 20 minutes, and had similar numbers in the Spanish League, getting a PIR of 16 in just 16 minutes. Rebounds, effectiveness, steals and very few missed shot should make Sedekerskis a player to consider. ### Braxton Key, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul (8.6 credits) After a great SuperCup semifinal against Real, [Braxton Key] keeps pacing Fenerbahce in all official competition. He led Fenerbahce to a 78-68 come back over Virtus with 11 points, 10 rebounds and a PIR of 22. In his first-ever Turkish League game, Key kept rolling with 12 points and 5 assists for a PIR of 18. It is hard to find a better bargain in the forward market right now! ### Konstantinos Mitoglou, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (5.5 credits) First things first, Panathinaikos is a T2 team in Rounds 2 and 3, which makes its good options even better. [Konstantinos Mitoglou] stepped on court for over 18 minutes to get 11 points, 6 rebounds and a couple of steals for a PIR of 14. At just 5.5 credits, he is a must-have player if he keeps posting those numbers. Oh, and keep an eye on [Eleftherios Mantzoukas] at just 4.8 credits, too.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Centers
text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] has just started! Not off to a good start? Don't worry, I am here to help you! You have four trades, so let's use them wisely. This may be the help you need to bounce back! Here's a quick review of my center picks from Round 1. Jonas Valanciunas was a slam dunk as he marked his return to the EuroLeague with 26.4 fantasy points and a gain of 0.4 credits. Kevarrius Hayes was also a clever pick as he went for 13.2 fantasy points and gained 0.2 credits, while Allan Dokossi was nearly as good with 12 fantasy points and a gain of 0.1 credits. Moses Wright hurt a lot of us with just 9 fantasy points, which caused him to lose 0.3 credits and I was too high on Austin Wiley, who ran into foul trouble, scored just 4.4 fantasy points and lost 0.3 credits. My advice is not limited to big men. Go see my [guard] and [forward] recommendations. Here is who I like at center in Round 2: ### Mathias Lessort, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (15.0 credits) It is a very simple decision to make: if you have the credits, you should go for [Mathias Lessort]. First, he is a T2 player, so if Vezen... if your captain doesn't play well, then you have a great choice with a very high floor. Lessort was at his very best in Round 1 with 15 points, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks and 9 fouls drawn against Paris. Who will stop him from now on? ### Dan Oturu, Hapoel Tel Aviv (14.9 credits) [Dan Oturu] had an outstanding first quarter against Bayern with 9 points and 8 rebounds. He looked on his way to be MVP of the Round, but slowed down and Hapoel didn't win. He finished that game with huge numbers: 20 points on 10-of-11 two-point shooting, 12 rebounds and 2 blocks for a PIR of 32. Oturu is Coach Itoudis's number one choice at center. He should be on your team. ### Olek Balcerowski, FC Barcelona (8.3 credits) If you need a cheaper option, then you can go for [Olek Balcerowski], who had a couple of really good performances last week. He opened the EuroLeague season with a bang: 10 points and 4 rebounds for a PIR of 14 against Efes. Balcerowski did even better in the Spanish League with 21 points and 6 rebounds for a PIR of 30. Josh Nebo is out, so it's Balcerowski's time in fantasy. ### Johannes Voigtmann, FC Bayern Munich (7.9 credits) Yes, Bayern plays against Fenerbahce, but it comes off a big win against Hapoel on [Johannes Voigtmann]'s go-ahead three-pointer. He made the most of his 19 minutes on the floor with 10 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists for a PIR of 17, while making few mistakes. Voigtmann has a lot of talent and experience, and comes off a game-winning shot. At his price, he is a good option. ### Kevarrius Hayes, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (7.5 credits) Last week, we talked about Partizan centers and how they would split minutes. Well, with Joffrey Lauvergne sidelined, [Kevarrius Hayes] and Tonye Jekiri are seeing more playing time and making the most of it. Hayes started in Round 1, finishing the game against Milan with 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting and 3 rebounds for a PIR of 12. Definitely not bad for 7.5 credits, right?

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Round 2: Who to hold, buy, or sell
text: The Round 1 of EuroLeague Fantasy is behind us, but after just one round, it is difficult to draw any definitive conclusions about players. A player’s performance and value can change significantly from round to round, so it is important to look at the bigger picture, including form, minutes, role within the team, and the upcoming schedule. That is why in this feature we will track EuroLeague players across the HOLD, BUY and SELL categories: players worth keeping, players whose value could rise, and players for whom it may be the right time to make a change. EuroLeague Fantasy Prices 2026-27: All 326 Player Credits HOLD Moses Wright – Milano – 13.7 credits Milano arguably boast the most favorable upcoming schedule in the entire EuroLeague. Over the next stretch, they will lock horns with Virtus, Baskonia, and Maccabi Tel Aviv – matchups where their frontcourt should flourish. While Moses Wright was completely contained in the opening round against Partizan and finished with a single-digit fantasy score, one quiet game does not alter his long-term outlook. He remains the central focal point around whom Milano’s tactical system will revolve this season. A massive number of fantasy managers placed their trust in him for Round 1, and selling him now would be premature. He is a primary hold for Round 2. Joel Parra – Barcelona – 6.7 credits Selected by roughly 30% of fantasy managers in the opening round, Joel Parra delivered a massive disappointment by finishing with zero fantasy points and suffering a 0.3 credit price drop. However, dropping him immediately based on a single outlier would be a mistake. Parra remains the premier budget option in his price range, slotted into a vital role as one of Barcelona’s primary anchors. Outside of that Round 1 bump, he consistently posted index ratings above 20 throughout preseason and Liga Endesa . His role and talent remain intact – hold him for Round 2 and expect a swift rebound. Arijan Lakic – Partizan – 4.0 credits Arijan Lakic is an absolute must-have asset at his minimum 4.0-credit valuation. Securing a baseline role of around 20 minutes per game at the basement price tier offers unparalleled roster flexibility. With Derek Willis sidelined, Partizan’s already depleted rotation shrinks even further, locking in Lakic’s court time and usage. His price tag is heavily insulated with massive upward mobility, making him a prime candidate to appreciate in market value. Holding him is a no-brainer until he approaches the 4.5 to 4.8 credit threshold – until then, keep him firmly locked in your lineup. EuroLeague Fantasy Round 2 Tips: Best Player Picks & Head Coaches BUY T.J. Shorts – Valencia – 15.1 credits Alongside Milano, Valencia hand managers one of the most enticing fixture runs over the next two rounds, locking horns with Baskonia at home before traveling to face Asvel. The up tempo, high-possessions game state expected in both encounters fits T.J. Shorts ’ game like a glove. If you passed on him in Round 1, bringing him in now is essential. He immediately demonstrated that Valencia is his team, taking full ownership as the focal offensive leader and engine. Expecting him to comfortably eclipse 20 fantasy points across both matchups is a realistic baseline given his dominant, high-usage workload. Dinos Mitoglou – Panathinaikos – 5.9 credits With Juancho Hernangomez questionable for the upcoming double round due to a groin issue, Panathinaikos’ already tight rotation upfront gets even thinner. That leaves head coach Zeljko Obradovic relying heavily on a frontcourt core of Mathias Lessort , Guerschon Yabusele , and Dinos Mitoglou . At a budget price tag of just 5.9 credits, Mitoglou represents extraordinary value. He is in line for an expanded role with a clear path to 20+ minutes of playing time while Panathinaikos navigate a highly favorable stretch of games. Given his scoring and rebounding potential, he is one of the top low-cost BUY targets on the market for Round 2. Mario Saint-Supery – Valencia – 4.9 credits Mario Saint-Supery stands out as another compelling Valencia player to target on the fantasy wire. Early rotation trends confirm that the young Spanish guard is firmly entrenched in the rotation, commanding a reliable 15 to 20 minutes of action per night. His affordable 4.9-credit price tag lowers the risk threshold significantly while delivering strong returns on minimal investment. Operating within an uptempo offense, he presents an ideal budget-enabler to anchor the end of your bench and free up critical capital for elite producers elsewhere. Buy him now before his valuation climbs. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Produce Well but Aren’t Fantasy Options SELL Jonas Valanciunas – Zalgiris – 15.9 credits Jonas Valanciunas was a dominant force against Crvena Zvezda in Round 1, imposing his will across the court to rack up a massive 26.4 fantasy points. Despite that explosive debut, selling him now is the smartest strategic move. Early signs suggest he experienced stamina fatigue early in that contest, raising valid durability concerns. With Zalgiris preparing to navigate demanding fixtures against fast-paced teams like Olympiacos and Paris, Valanciunas may struggle to match their relentless tempo. Moving on from him for the upcoming stretch allows you to reallocate premium capital into more sustainable, uptempo assets before reassessing his status later. Joel Bolomboy – Asvel – 10.2 credits Joel Bolomboy proved to be a major disappointment for fantasy managers in the opening round. Despite logging 26 minutes of action against Maccabi Tel Aviv, he remained virtually invisible on the offensive end, attempting a total of just two field goals throughout the contest. Early tactical signs indicate that he sits at the bottom of Asvel’s offensive hierarchy. Factor in a daunting road trip to face Panathinaikos in Round 2, and the writing is on the wall: now is the time to sell. Asvel’s fixture list eases up down the line, so if his offensive involvement picks up, he may re-emerge as a viable budget target later in the season. Bruno Fernando – Anadolu Efes – 10.0 credits Much like Joel Bolomboy, Bruno Fernando proved to be a major disappointment for fantasy managers in the opening round. He managed to scrape together just 3 fantasy points despite facing a shorthanded Barcelona frontcourt. With Anadolu Efes bracing for an exceptionally difficult schedule in the upcoming stretch, holding onto a center with low usage and minimal court time is an unnecessary liability. Fernando should be removed from your fantasy roster without second thought and replaced with higher-floor, more dependable options in his price tier. title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 2: Tuesday
text: Eight of Round 2's 10 games were played on Tuesday night, so the performance of players in those games on your [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] teams carries a lot of weight. Did you get the low-priced studs to boost your lineup? Did you get burned by high-priced flops? And nearly as important, who did those you compete against have? Let's break down which players sent your heart singing and which ones left you searching for a paper bag to cover your head with. Here are Tuesday’s fantasy winners and losers: ### Fantasy winners ### [Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna] What was I thinking! I researched Aliou Diarra. I believed in him. I had him on my roster for Round 1. And then I dropped him. What a fool I was! Diarra erupted for 15 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks, amassing a PIR of 22. If you are among the 2.1% of fantasy managers who had him, you got great value for a mere 6.6 credits. He’ll be more expensive by Round 3. ### [Dylan Osetkowski, Valencia Basket] A PIR of 20 is certainly not unheard of for Dylan Osetkowski, but it’s not common either. He had reached that number 4 times in 62 EuroLeague appearances entering this week. And then on Tuesday he scored 12 points on near-perfect shooting for a PIR of 20 off the bench in a blowout win over Baskonia. A fantastic performance for a 7.7-credit player. ### [Luca Vildoza, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade] With a line of 16 points and 6 steals, Luca Vildoza defied logic to help Partizan win in Paris. He earned 23.1 fantasy points for the 5.3% of owners bold enough to pay the 7.8-credit price tag on the Argentinian guard. It was the first time in 15 games that Vildoza had achieved a PIR of at least 20. How long until he does it again with Partizan? ### Fantasy losers ### [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Real Madrid] There is no way around it. If you were among the 5.4% of fantasy owners to roster Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot this week, you are in a bad place. It’s a trifecta of doom. His negative-10 PIR dooms your team this week. The fact that it came from a player you paid 12.4 credits for adds salt to the wound. And the relatively high loss in credits (it could be as high as a full credit!) you will see factored into TLC’s price before Round 3 dooms you a second time. Yikes! ### [Dario Brizuela, FC Barcelona] Oh, the fantasy gods can be so fickle! A week ago, we were celebrating those who had the foresight to pay 6.4 credits for Dario Brizuela as he racked up 17.6 fantasy points for just 6.4 credits. His price even rose 0.4 credits. Did you then sell him? Few did. Brizuela is owned by 8.9% of managers in Round 2 and he did not reward them. The Basque Mamba was held scoreless and posted a PIR of negative-8. Another tough pill to swallow. ### [Tyrique Jones, Olympiacos Piraeus] Sometimes fantasy owners (myself included) are naïve enough to think that when a star is sidelined, someone else can step into his minutes and perform. And sometimes we strike gold. Other times, we see Tyrique Jones give us 1.1 fantasy points after we paid 12.1 credits hoping he would dominate with Nikola Milutinov out. I say “we” to be kind. I didn’t make this mistake. But 2.2% of owners did. Better luck next time, my friends.

title: Patrick Baldwin Jr.’s EuroLeague debut remains on hold
text: By Nikola Miloradovic / info@eurohoops.net Patrick Baldwin Jr.’s wait for his EuroLeague debut will continue, with a back problem keeping him out of Crvena zvezda’s game against Anadolu Efes. The summer arrival from the NBA did not practice with the team, and coach Ibon Navarro said there is no clear timeline for his return. “ Baldwin didn’t practice with the team, and I don’t think he will play. I don’t know when he will return. He has a back problem and has undergone examinations. He practiced with the team two days ago and felt better, but he still doesn’t feel comfortable ,” Navarro said.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 2: Wednesday
text: - [Tuesday's Fantasy Challenge winners and losers] Just two games took place on Wednesday as Round 2 came to a close, and plenty of [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers were hoping to find a savior, or hoping their opponents didn't. Some smart managers found top performers at a cheap price; others watched their expensive bets flop. Here are Wednesday's Fantasy winners and losers from Round 2's second night. ### Fantasy winners ##### Devon Dotson, Besiktas Istanbul At 9.9 credits entering Round 2, [Devon Dotson] was priced as a mid-tier guard, but boy did he pay off for the 0.5% who had faith in him. He returned 26.4 fantasy points in Besiktas's 93-109 win at Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv. Expect his price to rise after this start to life in the EuroLeague. ##### Lefteris Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens At this point, it's no longer a surprise. [Lefteris Mantzoukas] would be a prime Breakout Fantasy Star candidate if that award existed. Valued at 4.8 credits entering Round 2, he finished with 20.9 Fantasy points in Panathinaikos's 102-79 win over LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne. Some 16.1% of you clearly heeded [Frankie and Javi's advice from the podcast]. Well done. ##### Nikos Rogkavopoulos, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens Mantzoukas got the acclaim, but [Nikos Rogkavopoulos] reminded everyone what he's capable of, finishing with 19.8 Fantasy points in the Greens' beatdown of ASVEL. The 6.1% who owned the 4.4-credit forward, despite him sitting out Round 1, must be feeling good about themselves, especially since I expected Konstantinos Mitoglou to be the one who broke out. ### Fantasy losers ##### Isaac Bonga, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens You'd expect [Isaac Bonga] to be a consistent fantasy performer at Panathinaikos, but that hasn't been the case: 1.1 points in Round 1, then 3.3 in Round 2. At 11.0 credits, the 5.6% who own him must be weighing whether to jump ship. Bonga's always been a better real-life player than a fantasy one, despite his improvement in fantasy last season, so his value could easily keep sliding. ##### Jae Crowder, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne Another pricey forward at 10.2 credits, [Jae Crowder] came back down to earth on Wednesday. After an impressive Round 1 debut, the 5.0% riding that wave got just 6.0 fantasy points as ASVEL fell at Panathinaikos. With a home game against Valencia Basket up next, it's worth watching if he bounces back. ##### Keaton Wallace, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv It's been a tricky start for [Keaton Wallace]. After -3 fantasy points in Round 1, at least 3.0 in Round 2 is progress, but not what you want from a 10.2-credit price tag. As a newbie, he's owned by just 0.6% of managers, and I don't expect that to climb until he finds his feet. There are better options at that cost, or cheaper.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 3: Centers
text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] is underway! Need to find a good trade? You got four of them, and I am here to help you with choosing a big man! Here's a quick review of my center picks from Round 2. Mathias Lessort shined with 24.2 points, and Olek Balcerowski had 15 fantasy points, which was a nice value pick since his price was 8.3 credits. Dan Oturu had 9.9 fantasy points, Johannes Voigtmann accumulated 8 points and Kevarrius Hayes was not my best pick, finishing with -0.9 fantasy points. My advice is not limited to big men, these are my [guard] recommendations, and forwards will be published later today. Here is who I like at center in Round 3: ### **Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas (16 credits)** You may think that Paris's fast-paced game might be too much for a big man like Valanciunas. Well, think again. He has been just unstoppable until now, averaging 12.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 2.0 blocks and a PIR of 22.5. Arvydas Sabonis's last season, 2003-04, was the one before we created the game. Is JV the closest thing to "Sabas" in fantasy? Probably! ### **Mathias Lessort, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (15.3 credits)** We don't like to repeat ourselves a lot, but if you don't have Lessort, it is probably bad for your fantasy team. Lessort is on a mission to outpower any other big man out there, and faces Maccabi, a team against he might feel he has something to prove. We know that the former player rule is not written in stone, but Lessort has been on fire lately and should keep going. ### **Marcus Bingham, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul (11.4 credits)** After showing hints of what he was able to do during the Euroleague Basketball SuperCup, Bingham had an excellent EuroLeague debut with Fenerbahce: 12 points on 5-of-7 shooting, 3 rebounds, 1 block and a PIR of 15 in less than 16 minutes. You can expect rebounds, a lot of blocked shots and an occasional three-pointer from now on. At his price, Bingham is a good choice. ### **Tonye Jekiri, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (9.2 credits)** That center situation in Partizan is hard to figure out but hey, we know this much: Jekiri is a very steady choice with a high floor. He will always get some rebounds, block one or two shots and score with good efficiency. In Paris, Jekiri had 15 points, seven rebounds and a PIR of 22, hitting 7-of-10 two-pointers. Despite Joffrey Lauvergne potentially returning, but Derek Willis still out, we like him. ### **Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna (7.2 credits)** EuroLeague Fantasy managers have been complaining to us for two weeks about the lack of cheap, good centers. Well, if that's your thing and you watched the Italian derby in Round 2, now you know one. Diarra finished the game with 15 points on 6-of-9 two-pointers, 7 rebounds, 4 blocks and a PIR of 22. He had a PIR of 10 against Fenerbahce in Round 1. Virtus's next opponent, Olympiacos, is without Nikola Milutinov.

Facing a struggling Asvel side, Shorts enters a favorable matchup where he should easily maintain this fast pace and deliver another 20+ fantasy point performance. He remains a premier guard pick for Round 3. Sylvain Francisco – Panathinaikos – 15.3 credits Sylvain Francisco put on a dominant display against his former club, Asvel, a team he signed with in the offseason but never actually played an official game for. He erupted for an impressive 27.5 fantasy points, proving that he is already stepped into the star role for Panathinaikos. With Kendrick Nunn sidelined, Francisco’s control over the offense becomes even more pronounced, raising both his usage rate and fantasy ceiling. As Panathinaikos prepare to host a vulnerable Maccabi Tel Aviv, expectations are high for another massive individual performance. He stands out as a elite backcourt option for Round 3. Carsen Edwards – Zalgiris – 11.4 credits Zalgiris travel to face Paris in a matchup that rarely sees Carsen Edwards featured as a recommended pick. However, this specific game is projected to feature a high tempo, rapid pace, and elevated scoring volume. With Nigel Williams-Goss unavailable, Edwards is set to shoulder a heavier usage rate and command increased ball-handling responsibilities in the backcourt. Facing a Paris defense that has struggled to contain perimeter scorers early in the season, he gains the volume and environment needed to generate strong value. Edwards represents an intriguing, high-upside guard option for Round 3. He produced a solid 13 fantasy points against Fenerbahce last time out, demonstrating clear progress in his physical sharpness and on-court comfort. Head coach Anton Gavel is continually increasing his responsibility, entrusting him with greater playmaking duties and extended minutes in Bayern’s backcourt rotation. At just 8.7 credits, Jokubaitis offers an affordable pathway to reliable production, making him a strong budget target for Round 3 managers seeking upside. Matteo Spagnolo – Baskonia – 6.3 credits Baskonia enter a manageable stretch of fixtures featuring high-tempo opponents like Milano, Besiktas, and Dubai. These upcoming games are expected to produce high scoring totals and abundant offensive possessions, making a long-term investment in a Baskonia player a smart strategic move for fantasy managers. Italian guard Matteo Spagnolo stands out as an ideal candidate due to his modest 6.3 credit valuation. Operating in a system that rewards dynamic guard play, Spagnolo should have minimal trouble outperforming his bargain price tag and delivering strong value relative to his cost. He is a high-upside budget option for Round 3 and beyond. Best options under 6.0 credits Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada – Asvel – 5 credits Asvel possess one of the most fantasy-friendly schedules over the next few rounds, lining up matchups against high-tempo sides like Valencia and Paris. Both opponents routinely push the pace and play at an elevated possession count, creating a fertile environment for fantasy accumulation. Guard Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada has carved out an unexpectedly important role in Asvel’s rotation early in the campaign, earning consistent minutes and ball-handling duties. Priced at the absolute minimum of 5.0 credits, he provides essential salary relief while offering genuine box-score contribution. He is a prime budget enabler for Round 3. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Will Have Smaller Roles Compared to Their Previous Teams Forwards Best options over 10.0 credits Guerschon Yabusele – Panathinaikos – 14.2 credits Guerschon Yabusele appears to still be adjusting to his role within the Panathinaikos system, though he has rarely been forced into top gear during the opening two rounds. Facing a high-stakes matchup, Yabusele gains a prime platform to showcase his full fantasy capabilities, making him an attractive elite forward option for Round 3. Because Crvena Zvezda rely so heavily on his shot-creation and wing versatility, a turnaround in their record directly hinges on getting him back to form. Facing his former club Anadolu Efes provides extra personal motivation to step up and carry the scoring load. Expect Nwora to deliver a strong bounce-back performance and produce high fantasy value in Round 3.
