title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 3: Guards
text: With Round 2 in the books, it is time for a quick turnaround as Round 3 of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] already tips off tonight. Here's a quick review of my guard recommendations from Round 2. Carlik Jones had 28.6 fantasy points and Sylvain Francisco finished with 27.5, both turned out as great selections. So was Scottie Wilbekin who had 19.8 points, a great value with his price of 7.7 credits. On the other end of the spectrum, Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada had -1 fantasy points in Round 3, and Dovydas Giedraitis finished with -2. My advice is not limited to guards, also check out my [center] recommendations, and a short list of forwards will be published later today. Here is who I like at guard in Round 3: ### **Scottie Wilbekin, Besiktas Istanbul (8.2 credits)** After playing just seven EuroLeague games in the last two seasons, Wilbekin is back to the player that fans used to love and opponents used to fear. Wilbekin had a great game against one of his former teams, Maccabi, finishing it with 20 points on 4-of-5 three-pointers, three assists and a PIR of 18 in less than 23 minutes. Right now, Wilbekin is a big bargain in the game. ### **Luca Vildoza, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (8.4 credits)** It has been a while since we last saw a EuroLeague player collect 10 steals in the opening two games of the competition. Despite coming off the bench, Vildoza is really posting solid numbers: 11.5 points on 85.7% three-pointers, 2.5 assists, 5.0 steals and a PIR of 15.0. He plays against FC Bayern Munich in Round 3. Just go for him. ### **Theo Maledon, Real Madrid (10 credits)** It is a bit surprising to see Real at 0-2 right now, and this is exactly why I think *Los Blancos* players should be considered in Round 3. The team faces Hapoel in Sofia, it is a rematch of last season's playoff series, and Maledon has been playing well so far, averaging 10.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.5 fouls drawn for a PIR average of 14.0. Players with all-around contributions always pay off. ### **Sterling Brown, Zalgiris Kaunas (10.7 credits)** We spoke about Zalgiris's guard situation before Round 2. Well, Dovydas Giedraitis and Maodo Lo each had a negative PIR, Carsen Edwards had a solid game and Brown was the only player who overperformed. We could expect more or less the same as Zalgiris visits fast-paced Paris in Round 3. He averaged a PIR of 18.5 in two games against Paris last season, better than his season average of 11.0. ### **TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket (15.3 credits)** Valencia set a new all-time scoring club record, getting 111 points against Baskonia, and should keep pushing the pedal against ASVEL. Shorts had 10 assists and just one turnovers in Round 2, getting a PIR of 20 while taking only eight field goal attempts. Going back to France should bring Shorts good memories, and that makes him even more attractive, a top-class choice.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 3: Forwards
text: There's barely been time to catch a breath before Round 3 of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] tips off. My advice isn't limited to forwards. Also check out my [guard] and [center] recommendations for Round 3. Here are the forwards I like in Round 3: ### Lefteris Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens I mean, this is a no-brainer. No cheap player is doing better than [Lefteris Mantzoukas], who has been absolutely extraordinary so far. In two games, he's averaging 13.0 points on 4-of-4 two-point shooting and 6-of-12 from three, 5.0 rebounds and a PIR of 15.5. He's been starting at power forward and making the most of his opportunity. If you don't have Mantzoukas, buy him now. ### Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas [Azuolas Tubelis] is still a bargain for his price range and has been excellent. His speed, high basketball IQ and versatility make him a perfect matchup against Paris, where he recorded his first career double-double last season. He's now averaging 14.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists and a PIR of 22.5, and should keep helping Zalgiris all season long. ### Tadas Sedekerskis, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz It's good to see [Tadas Sedekerskis] fully healthy and playing like the effective player he's always been. He proved it against Valencia despite his team's 23-point loss, posting 16 points on 8-of-8 two-point shooting, seven rebounds and a PIR of 19 in just 22 minutes. Baskonia is set to bounce back at home in the Buesa Arena, and if that happens, Sedekerskis should be a big part of it. ### Jason Burnell, Armani Olimpia Milan There aren't too many mid-range options around 10 credits, so I'm finishing this piece with two of them. [Jason Burnell] had a rock-solid game in the Italian derby, with six points and 10 rebounds in under 17 minutes. Expect him to keep crashing the glass, playing with energy and hitting free throws to put together a solid PIR most nights. ### Conor Morgan, Besiktas Istanbul [Conor Morgan] looks confident in Besiktas's system, starting at power forward to pull the trigger from downtown and finish dunks off backdoor cuts. He's averaging 14.0 points on excellent shooting (80.0% on twos, 60.0% on threes), 2.5 rebounds and a PIR of 13.5. As long as he keeps finding good shots, Morgan will keep knocking most of them down.

title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 3: Thursday
text: There were some monster performances on Thursday night and I hope you had some of the authors of those games on your [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. Of course, there were some stinkers, too. I hope you avoided those pitfalls. Here's a look at the best and worst of Thursday's performances: ### Fantasy winners ### [Theo Maledon, Real Madrid] To get 40 fantasy points is fantastic regardless of the price. To get it from a player who cost just 10 credits is amazing. That is what Theo Maledon did for the 9.2% of managers who invested in him this week. I am going to go out on a limb and say that most of the top scores in fantasy for Round 3 will come from managers who had Maledon, whose price is certain to rise before Round 4. ### [Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna] I am pretty certain that the number of fantasy managers who own Aliou Diarra is going to rise a lot in the next few days. It was 5.8% for Round 3. The Virtus center had a PIR of 22 in Round 2. Then he went off for 18 points and 14 rebounds for a fantasy score of 33 on Thursday. That’s a magnificent return for a center who cost 7.2 credits. ### [Mbaye Ndiaye, Olympiacos Piraeus] The athletic big man seems to have found a groove with Olympiacos and despite playing just 20 minutes off the bench, Mbaye Ndiaye scored 23 points on near-perfect shooting and grabbed 7 rebounds for a PIR of 29. That’s incredible value for the price of 7.5 credits. Congratulations to the 2.0% of managers who had Ndiaye for Round 3. #### Honorable mention: ### [Ognjen Dobric, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] It’s hard to put Ognjen Dobric in the same category as the other winners, who scored on average more than double what the Zvezda forward mustered. That said, Dobric cost much less (4.5 credits) and was owned by 5.9% of owners. That makes his 15.4 fantasy points pretty valuable! ### Fantasy losers ### Olympiacos Piraeus centers Nothing hurts fantasy managers more than foul trouble. [Tyrique Jones] got into foul trouble and barely played, featuring for a total of 3:22 minutes. He committed 4 fouls and that ended up in a PIR of negative-4. That is a crippling score for a center priced at 11.6 credits. At least Jones was only taken by 2.1% of owners. His fellow Olympiacos center [Donta Hall] is owned by 5.8% of owners and posted a negative-6! ### [Jared Butler, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] While Crvena Zvezda held odd Efes for the win, some of their key rotation players struggled and hurt their fantasy managers too. Jared Butler was the second-most owned Zvezda player at 8.5% and with a price 10.3 credits, his managers were surely confident that the second-year guard was going to deliver a lot more than a PIR on negative-2. His backcourt mate, [Chris Jones], came into Round 3 owned by 4.4% of managers, who paid 12.3 credits for him. Jones, though, hurt them with a score of 0. ### [Andres Feliz, Real Madrid] The Dominican slugger was a bit of a sleeper pick for some after averaging 9.5 points, 4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in his first two games. It sounded like a bargain for just 6.6 credits. So 14.8% of fantasy managers gave Andres Feliz a spot in their lineups for Round 3. And then he bottomed out with a negative-4 in the loss to Hapoel.

title: Μάικ Τζέιμς: Επιβεβαιώθηκε το χειρότερο σενάριο, ζημιά στον αχίλλειο
text: Μεγάλη απώλεια για την Αναντολού Εφές, καθώς ο Μάικ Τζειμς θα μείνει εκτός παρκέ για τους επόμενους 7-9 μήνες. Ο Αμερικανός μπασκετμπολίστας υπέστη ζημιά στον αχίλλειο τένοντα και θα περάσει άμεσα την πόρτα του χειρουργείου για να αποκατασταθεί το πρόβλημα. Θυμίζουμε ότι ο Μάικ Τζειμς τραυματίστηκε κατά τη διάρκεια της αναμέτρησης Ερυθρός Αστέρας – Αναντολού Εφές και αποχώρησε από το παρκέ με φορείο στο τέλος της τρίτης περιόδου.

title: Παναθηναϊκός: Απρόοπτο με Ρογκαβόπουλο
text: Την ώρα που επέστρεψε στη διάθεση του Ζέλικο Ομπράντοβιτς ο Νάιτζελ Χέις – Ντέιβις , η ατυχία χτύπησε ξανά την πόρτα του Παναθηναϊκού. text: Ο Γκέρσον Γιαμπουσέλε με 17 πόντους αναδείχτηκε πρώτος σκόρερ στη νίκη του Παναθηναϊκού στο παιχνίδι με τη Μακάμπι Τελ Αβίβ . title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 3: Friday
text: Round 3's Friday night slate delivered a stunning comeback, a coaching nightmare, and one of the cheapest buys of the season so far for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers. Here are my fantasy winners and losers from the action. ### Fantasy winners ##### Nikola Mirotic, Valencia Basket Signed as a late addition, [Nikola Mirotic] has looked right at home at Valencia, and fantasy-wise, he's back to his best. In the club's stunning comeback win at LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne, he posted 26.4 fantasy points, his highest total of the season, while climbing into third on the EuroLeague's all-time scoring list past Vassilis Spanoulis. Just 2.9% of fantasy managers have him on their rosters, and they're looking smart right now. ##### Patty Mills, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne Javier Gancedo had his "Dzanan Musa rule" for games in Bosnia and Herzegovina last season. Maybe it's time for a "[Patty Mills] rule" at LDLC Arena. Owned by just 1.8% of fantasy managers, the veteran guard finished with 25.0 fantasy points in Round 3, following 19.8 in Round 1 (also at home) and 9.0 in Round 2 (on the road). The pattern speaks for itself. ##### Marcus Bingham, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul The 0.8% of fantasy managers who heeded Javier Gancedo's advice in [his Fantasy Tips article] by rostering [Marcus Bingham] knew what they were doing. The Fenerbahce center erupted for 27.5 fantasy points on Friday night, making his 11.4-credit price tag look like a steal. Let's see if managers hold on to him for a trip to Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens next week. ### Fantasy losers ##### Oded Kattash, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv This is the first time I've featured a coach in the fantasy winners and losers column, but things have gone from bad to worse for Maccabi tactician Oded Kattash. A 90-67 drubbing on the road at Panathinaikos brought him -20 fantasy points, the worst mark of any coach in Round 3, following -10 in Round 2 and -5 in Round 1. The 4.6% of fantasy managers hoping for a miracle on Friday night ended up with egg on their faces. ##### Jaylen Hoard, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv At 14.7 credits, [Jaylen Hoard] was one of the most expensive forwards in fantasy heading into Round 3, so his -2.0 fantasy points was a big disappointment for the 1.1% of managers who had him on their rosters. Hoard has been a reliable option in past seasons, but his trajectory since a 20.0-point haul in Round 1 is worrying. ##### David DeJulius, Besiktas Istanbul It wasn't [David DeJulius]'s night against FC Barcelona, as he finished with -3.0 fantasy points in his team's home defeat. His 9.6-credit price looked enticing entering Round 3, even though he didn't feature in Round 2, but the 0.5% of fantasy managers who went for him will be regretting it.
